sections.title: Effort after you can already win

items.q: What does 'work is the goal' replace?
items.a: The score — even 'the score takes care of itself' still worships the score. After you can win, **effort conditional on winning is too low**. Only you know the private grade. Public win can still be a **private loss**.

items.q: What is on Hormozi's wall besides the good-day formula?
items.a: **Focus is subtraction.** Dorsey: perfect the details, **limit the number**. The team should feel better because you told them what **not** to do. AI-maxing a dumb initiative is negative subtraction.

sections.title: The swamp and how you leave it

items.a: Personal needs are met. The next real hire or ad-spend jump is **half of profit**. It took some risk to enter; it takes **more risk to leave**. Most stay stuck — arguably rationally.

items.q: What three levers raise output without a heroic hire?
items.a: **Demand** (customer → content → more customers), **conversion** (one-to-many + preload so reps make 6-inch putts), **delivery** (async, batched, recorded, remote, one-to-many). Common sense first; AI second.

items.q: What do Getty, Rockefeller, and Musk keep doing at local maximums?
items.a: Push **chips back in the middle**. Risk tolerance has to grow with the stack or the game dies. Nest egg first so the worst case is your **day does not change**.

items.q: When do you stop building businesses?
items.a: After enough failed first salespeople and managers you **assemble** them: known parts + a Rolodex. Failure writes the pattern library. Filter: **what changes about my day?**
